newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO TAKE NO NEW MEASURES IN 1997- ECON MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO TAKE NO NEW MEASURES IN 1997- ECON MIN.

text.p: Greece's fiscal adjustment is on track and there is no need for new measures, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou told reporters on Tuesday.
"Absolutely no new measure is going to be taken," said Papandoniou who pointed out that the budget deficit was on target and there was improvement in inflation in 1997.

Greece's CPI inflation firmed to 5.5 percent year-on-year in June from 5.4 percent in May. The general government budget deficit is projected to drop to 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 from 7.4 percent in 1996.

Provisional government figures showed that the budget deficit was on target in the first half of this year. Revenues rose 17.5 percent year-on-year helped by OTE telecom's part-flotation proceeds. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
